claimAlignment.claim: Output is measured directly, not inferred from the plotted model.
claimAlignment.evidence: T-piece diverts arterial blood into a graduated vessel; filling time measured with a stop-watch.

claimAlignment.claim: Venous and arterial load controls are different.
claimAlignment.evidence: Early experiments changed reservoir height; later ones opened the venous clip at reservoir height around35cm. Arterial resistance was a thin rubber tube controlled by external air pressure.

claimAlignment.claim: Within working limits output follows inflow and per-beat output depends on filling.
claimAlignment.evidence: Steady circulation must return the entering blood; the authors explicitly connect per-beat output with diastolic filling, then describe maximal distension and failure.

claimAlignment.claim: Raised afterload does not mean the same experiment as fixed venous pressure.
claimAlignment.evidence: At given inflow the arterial resistance changes required venous pressure and residual volume. The plotted modern model holds filling pressure independently.

claimAlignment.claim: Isolation does not eliminate circulating hormones or reproduce intact-animal pressure conditions.
claimAlignment.evidence: Intrathoracic pressure differences and clinical extrapolation limitations are explicit; TablesIV/V include adrenaline.
